def: Fluent, plausible model output that is not supported by the facts of the world or by the material the model was given.
An output that conflicts with facts about the world, either by inventing something or by misstating a real fact.
An output that conflicts with what the user supplied, such as a summary that contradicts or adds to its source document.
Inventing an entity, case, paper, quotation or function that does not exist.
The share of training mentions whose fact appears exactly once, which estimates how much probability lies on facts the model cannot tell from unseen ones.
A model whose stated confidence matches how often it is actually right.
A model committing to an early mistake and then producing further errors to stay consistent with it.
A model declining to answer, for example by saying it does not know, instead of guessing.
Scoring each answer as right (1) or not right (0), which gives no credit for abstaining and so rewards guessing.
A short statement containing one piece of information, used as the unit when scoring long-form text for factual precision.
The percentage of a generation's atomic facts that a reliable knowledge source supports.
A short-form factuality benchmark whose answers are graded correct, incorrect or not attempted.
